purpose.summary: Add a canonical confirmed-token query core for the persistent ALP/SLP index and a bounded internal C ABI without registering a public service.
scope: Reuse the public Bitcoin ABC Chronik token-query representation for confirmed token genesis metadata and return the canonical TokenInfo protobuf.
Persist the accepted block-header timestamp needed by canonical confirmed block metadata.
Expose a panic-contained two-pass C ABI that reports the exact payload size before copying into a caller-owned buffer.
Cover ALP and SLP token types, absent and non-genesis transactions, restart-safe database reads, exact rollback, invalid pointers and undersized buffers.
exclusions: No socket, HTTP route, RPC, websocket, mempool query, wallet integration or public service is added.
No consensus, validation, activation, chain-selection, P2P, network-identity or mainnet parameter behavior changes.
No private source, history, operator data, incoming evidence, binary, cache, build output or host-specific path is tracked.

commands: Build the standalone node with all Chronik options OFF.
expected_results: The query code is absent from the executable link graph and node behavior remains unchanged.

commands: Build bitcoind and the observer tests with BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=ON while leaving runtime opt-in disabled.
expected_results: The internal protobuf boundary links and tests pass without registering or opening Chronik state.

commands: Run the locked offline Rust corpus and the existing local-regtest observer matrix with explicit opt-in.
expected_results: Confirmed ALP/SLP genesis metadata is queryable internally and indexing remains isolated from node correctness.

scenarios.command: Run the asset observer scenario and the token query unit boundary.
expected_results: Explicit opt-in indexes accepted ALP/SLP state and returns canonical confirmed token metadata.
failure_conditions: Implicit enablement, malformed payload acceptance, wrong token metadata, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Restart the explicit local-regtest index and repeat the confirmed token query.
expected_results: The token and its canonical block metadata remain readable after restart.
failure_conditions: Missing token, timestamp drift, path leakage, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the existing full-reindex observer scenario before querying confirmed metadata.
expected_results: A rebuilt index returns the same canonical confirmed token representation.
failure_conditions: Stale state, incomplete rebuild, query divergence, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the existing chainstate-reindex observer scenario before querying confirmed metadata.
expected_results: Ordered callbacks rebuild queryable state without changing chain selection.
failure_conditions: Stale state, node-authority effect, query divergence, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the existing pruned-datadir observer scenario.
expected_results: Unavailable history disables only persistence; no query can silently serve contradictory state.
failure_conditions: Node shutdown, silent stale query, validation effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run exact-tip rollback and deep-reorganization failure scenarios, then query the rolled-back token ID.
expected_results: Rolled-back token metadata is absent and contradictions remain isolated to indexing.
failure_conditions: Stale token response, silent corruption, node-authority effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

limitations: This change creates only an internal confirmed-token query boundary; no user-visible API or service exists yet.
Mempool token information, Avalanche finality, transaction queries, UTXOs, histories and websocket subscriptions remain outside this slice.
The local macOS run is a component observation only; public CI and review are still pending.
counterevidence: The first local native build attempt could not load libclang until the Xcode toolchain library directory was supplied explicitly; the governed build already documents this dependency.
An undersized output buffer is deliberately rejected without writing any byte, and an unknown or non-genesis transaction deliberately returns no token result.
The imported full Chronik HTTP and indexer crates remain excluded because this slice reuses only the confirmed token representation required by the accepted runtime.
